results.content: Alaska's numbers are less severe but still soft for a state he carried by 13 points less than two years ago. A Morning Consult tracking poll put his net approval in the state at minus 5, worse than deep-red Wyoming but nowhere close to the minus-41 Morning Consult recorded in Vermont. Civiqs data through early June put his approval in Alaska at 43 percent, disapproval at 51 percent.

About a year and a half into his second term, President Donald Trump's approval rating among Utah voters continues to be underwater.

A new Deseret News/Hinckley Institute of Politics poll, conducted by Morning Consult, found Utahns generally aren't happy with the way Trump has handled his return to the White House. It's a trend seen in nationwide polling, too, despite the president boasting about positive ratings. [...] While Utahns are fairly evenly split about whether they approve or disapprove of Trump's performance, survey data going back to January paints a different picture.
